slow-queries.description: Slow log thresholds are set unreasonably low (1ms warn, 0ms info) and several query patterns are inherently expensive

problems.impact: Every single query logs as slow. Fills up logs, obscures real performance issues, adds I/O overhead.
problems.fix: Raise thresholds: warn=1s, info=200ms (or disable info-level slow log entirely)

problems.impact: Leading wildcards cannot use the inverted index. Forces a full scan of every term in the field. O(n) where n = unique terms.
problems.fix: Use match query with appropriate analyzer, or use ngram tokenizer if substring search is required. If wildcard is necessary, avoid leading *.

problems.evidence: script_score with match_all and Math.log computation
problems.impact: Executes script on every document in the index. No index optimization possible. CPU-bound O(n).
problems.fix: Pre-compute the score at index time into a dedicated field. Or use function_score with field_value_factor instead of custom script.

problems.impact: ES must fetch and score 10,010 documents across all shards, discard 10,000. Memory and CPU waste scales linearly with 'from'.
problems.fix: Use search_after for deep pagination, or point-in-time API. Avoid from > 10000 (default max_result_window).

problems.evidence: terms aggregation on trace_id with size=100000
problems.impact: trace_id is high cardinality (unique per request). Aggregating 100k buckets requires large amounts of memory. Response payload is massive.
problems.fix: Reduce size to a reasonable limit (10-100). Use composite aggregation for paginated access to all buckets. Consider if this aggregation is actually needed.
